summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of liver transplant, chronic kidney disease, severe malnutrition, and prior colon cancer, was admitted for acute abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and worsening watery diarrhea. He was found to have C. difficile infection confirmed by positive stool PCR and toxin assay. A CT scan revealed malpositioning of his GJ tube, which was contributing to symptoms. He underwent successful GJ tube exchange and was treated with a 14-day course of oral vancomycin. Acute kidney injury improved with IV fluids, and nutritional support was restored via the new feeding tube. He progressed to a regular diet, remained stable, and was discharged home with instructions to complete antibiotics, resume home nursing care for tube feeds, and follow up with his primary and transplant teams.
